items.content_html:
The Past

In 2024, Huihui officially began HRT, but faced strong opposition from her family. She began self-harming and experiencing overdoses… After being rescued, she was sent by her family to a psychiatric hospital. There, she was subjected to involuntary treatment in violation of regulations for a month, leaving her with severe psychological trauma. She eventually chose to leave on her own and went to Guangxi to live with her boyfriend.

After a period of happiness together, they eventually broke up because of various difficulties in their lives. Huihui then spent some time living alone in Beihai, struggling with loneliness.

First Met

By the time I met Huihui, it was already April 2026. You could say I came into her life rather late, and that is something I still regret…

At the time, Huihui had been taken to the hospital after self-harming. Her wounds had not healed properly, but the hospital was unwilling to treat them any further. After discussing it again and again, I offered her two options: “Go home, or wait a few more days. Once I’m on holiday, I’ll come and help you find a place to rent together.”

Huihui chose to go home. Her diary later revealed that she had chosen to return home because she knew she might hurt herself again, and she didn’t want to make me worry.

After Huihui went home, I continued to stay with her online. I also helped her repay her loans, and she found a job and worked hard to pay me back. But the job was simply too exhausting, and she eventually quit.

After everything she had been through over those two years, she came to understand what she truly wanted:

“I just want to be loved.”

Final Chapter

But after returning home, Huihui was confined to the house by her family and was not allowed to travel far. She could only play VRChat and meet some of her friends nearby to ease the pain. (Sigh… there was really so little I could do for her from behind a screen.)

After we spent some time trying to find work together, Huihui still had no choice but to return home. Finding a job was not easy. She had tried so hard for so long, but ultimately, nothing came of it.

After returning home, she also had to endure constant criticism and pressure from her family. Even VRChat gradually became unable to give Huihui enough reason to keep going.

Finally, on August 2, 2026, she chose to leave.

The night before, I was still chatting with Huihui:

“Remember to call me when you wake up tomorrow.”

But the next morning, there was nothing but an endless ringing tone on the other end of the phone. In our private messages was the final post she sent to me…

Before she left, she had mailed me her final gift, along with the belongings she left behind.

This time, I couldn’t hold on to her either.

I’m sorry.

I want to do one last thing for Huihui.

Huihui was a very kind person. She was always encouraging others online to keep living.

Her only wish was to have companionship and love.

She was willing to give so much to others, hoping only that someone would treat her with the same kindness in return.

Sadly, that never happened.

There was a passage in the diary she left behind:

Cherish those who treat you well.

If you ever lose them,

you may never get them back.

Please cherish them, everyone.

Live well. Cherish those around you.

In memory of Huihui

…

Contributor for this entry: Tsukino Shion

items.content_html:
Farewell, Yukikaze

Today, the person we are saying goodbye to is named Yukikaze.

When she left this world, she was less than a month away from her seventeenth birthday. But she did not live to see it.

I often think that people like us are born without a passport, never given the right to apply for one, carrying only a temporary residence permit. Yukikaze simply could not keep applying anymore. She had grown weary of the endless journey from one door to another.

But what kind of person was Yukikaze? Like everyone here, she had a heart of gold. She was kind, she spread love and warmth, and she tried with all her might to love this world, even though this world never truly loved her in return.

Today, I found her lover and learned all of this:

On February 22nd of this year, they met each other. They lived on the same street, just a few hundred steps apart. They attended the same middle school, just two grades apart.

At 3 PM on March 1st, they met offline for the first time. Yukikaze gave her a fishcake keychain[^1] and bought her a pink Monster Energy drink. When it was time to leave the arcade, Yukikaze rode her electric scooter to take her home. Downstairs at her apartment, Yukikaze hugged her for the first time. She said that warmth… it was so incredibly warm.

Every weekend after that, they could be found at the arcade near their homes. From the two of them huddling together chatting, to holding hands, hugging, and pressing their cheeks together.

In April, they got matching glasses frames. On May 4th, they took the subway together to Guangzhou for the first time, strolling through ComiCity and going to the Firefly ACG Expo. On her birthday, May 19th, she made just one wish: to stay with her older sister forever, and never be separated.

During the Dragon Boat Festival in June, Yukikaze said she was going back to Anhui. She cried, and Yukikaze comforted her. But Yukikaze was also sick—even though she was simultaneously a crisis intervention volunteer. Sleeping at midnight and waking up at 6 AM, her family had smashed her phone and computer, refusing to let her go to the hospital, so she could only obtain raw lithium carbonate herself, without being able to seek proper medical care. Throughout the entire semester, Yukikaze carried the emotional burdens of others, her own illness, and the knives waiting for her at home.

She carried far too many things she shouldn’t have had to. Yet she never stopped loving others, never stopped reaching out to pull someone up.

After the high school entrance exams, Yukikaze decided to accompany her until July 15th. They went to the Apple Store, Starbucks, IKEA, and wandered all over Foshan. Once, in a hospital corridor, Yukikaze said her wish was to obtain her gender dysphoria diagnosis after coming of age, and save money for gender-affirming surgery. That day, she confessed her feelings to Yukikaze. She said Yukikaze had become closer to her than a sister could ever be.

July 14th, the last day. They went to the largest square, walking hand in hand, kissing and hugging in empty corners, sharing the same bowl of sweet dessert soup.

On the way back, sitting on the backseat of Yukikaze’s scooter, she said:

“Let’s be together.”

Yukikaze nodded.

“We’re sisters, and we’re girlfriends too.”

They laughed so loudly that day. Downstairs at her apartment, Yukikaze handed her a box of gifts—anime badges, skincare products, and two blank CDs. Then Yukikaze rode away. She watched that fading silhouette, not knowing it would be the last time she ever saw her.

Yukikaze said she would wait for her to return, but ultimately broke her promise.

I think of the letters Chiu Miao-chin wrote during her final days in Paris. Every word seemed to say: I tried, but this world gave me no place to stand.

Yukikaze was the same. It wasn’t that she didn’t love her; she loved her too much, loved her until she couldn’t hold on anymore.

Yukikaze’s lover said:

“The younger sister has always loved her older sister. From the first meeting to her departure, from being together to being separated, I loved her every single moment. No matter if the older sister is a biological sister or something else in the younger sister’s heart, she is the person the younger sister cherishes the most in this life. At least right now, the older sister is the most precious, the most valued person. She will always be the most important person. The younger sister will never forget her older sister. Those memories will always be there; they will always be beautiful memories.”

I want to say to Yukikaze: Sixteen years, you owe no one. You left, and I do not blame you. But the next time you come, remember to find a world that has gotten better, good enough that you can stay.

The pastor said: Her identity is not a sin, her love is not a mistake. The Lord knows her as she truly is.

The priest said: She has returned to the light, and there shall be no more tears.

Yukikaze is gone. But we are still here. We live, not to atone for sins, but to prove—this world was not worthy of the price she paid, but we are worthy of living.

We must live to see seventeen, eighteen, twenty, and beyond, for her. We must wear pretty clothes for her, eat sweet things for her, and hear our names spoken correctly for her. Live for her, until no more of our kind have to die just for being themselves.

Yukikaze, Maomao, Xiao Chen, Susu, Tangtang.

They are not isolated tragedies. For a child to be themselves, they have to climb over the walls of family, school, society, law, and healthcare—every single wall. Some make it over, and some remain forever at the foot of the wall. We are not mourning death; we are mourning that this world has not yet learned to be gentle.

On behalf of Yukikaze’s lover, and all those who could not come, I thank you. Thank you for not turning away, thank you for speaking her name. She has not disappeared; she lives on in your words.

Today, it is not only Yukikaze whom we have lost. We have lost too many others like her. Every one of us who is alive must help each other, support each other, and survive together. Living is victory. We must live well for her, and live well for all of our kind who have passed away. Our togetherness is the longest echo she leaves behind in this world.

We are creating a tomorrow, we are living for tomorrow, we keep fighting, we keep moving forward, and our tomorrow will be bathed in sunlight, full of light!

Today is Sunday. Time passes so quickly, and seven days have already carried the tide of life toward the far horizon. I want to gently touch the sea, and watch the paper planes drift into the distance. Please, let the breeze keep blowing. Let it follow the sea to the horizon. Remember to look back. There is a child waiting at the pier, waiting for the promised meeting. Bring back the birds, light as air, smell the breath of spring, circle the streets, and listen to the noise of the city.

Gently touch the sea… gently touch the sea… a child is looking out at the pier…

Yukikaze. You are free. You are home. We love you. We will not forget.

Dedicated to Yukikaze (August 12, 2009 - July 17, 2026)

Comrade Xiaozhi, a transgender person, written at 1:00 AM on July 18, 2026.

[^1]: Fishcake: Here it refers to a keychain featuring the “Narutomaki” (🍥) design. Because its pattern resembles the appearance of “Progynova”, an estrogen medication commonly used by transgender women, it is often used by the transgender community in mainland China as a subtle symbol for identity and mutual recognition.

items.summary: You are free. You are home. We love you. We will not forget.

items.content_html:
Maybe I’d be better off dating the J-20 and J-16 (?)

—— CEFINE, 2024-02-15 13:12

Profile

Every time I scrolled through Nimao’s profile, the first thing I would definitely see was a notification that he had changed his avatar.

Judging from the very few bio statuses he left behind, he was probably a kid who really liked mecha girls and gun girls; just like the quote above, which was also a part of his bio.

No one could have imagined that someone so optimistic, who hung out in group chats every day and spent so much time surfing the web, bringing endless warmth to his friends, was enduring immense physical and psychological pressure behind the screen…

Memories

By: _AloneStar_

He and I had known each other quite a long time. As of today, he had been on my friends list for four years, but I didn’t know him all that well. He seemed to never mention a word about his real life. However, I do recall him mentioning his illness once.

In short, he said he would probably lose his ability to take care of himself soon. He was such a poor kid... Yet he still chatted in groups and played games every day as usual. He didn’t seem anxious about it at all, and occasionally even shared some nice pictures in the group. You couldn’t tell at all that he was a kid with a terminal illness.

By: Arista

Nimao was a very interesting and fun person... I’m not good at describing my feelings, but in short, he was just a really fun person. During the time we spent together, he brought me endless joy. “Fun” is the highest praise I can give him.

“We’ll Meet Again Tomorrow” By: Heibuzai

It feels a bit late to be writing this.

Nimao, I used to call you Maomao (Cat). You used to go by Maomao, after all, and I don't know when you started being called Nimao.

You were one of the earliest friends I ever made on QQ. I can’t quite remember how long we had known each other, and it’s no longer visible in the friend details anymore, because there was a period when I deleted a lot of my friends out of spite. I felt like none of you cared about me, and thought that maybe doing that would get your attention. It was childish.

A very long time ago, you were the one who added me and invited me to play with you. I was so happy. I really liked you, and even now I still remember all those times we spent playing Minecraft together. But perhaps because of that, I felt the distance between us even more. In the little world of QQ, you were always surrounded by so many people, and little by little, I felt myself being pushed out of your sight. Maybe it was just my own mind playing tricks on me, but I felt like you weren’t as close to me as you used to be…

I tried my best to fit into your world, learning about the games you played and getting to know your friends, even though I was a little clumsy at it. But you left, on July 3rd.

You know, I miss you so much. I don’t know what place I held in your heart, or what colour I was there. But Maomao, in my heart, you were never just an ordinary online friend. Ever since I first got into QQ as a social platform, you were one of the most colourful, and one of the most important friends I had ever met there. Perhaps we may never know who you really were behind the screen, but we will always know “Nimaomao”.

I don’t know how others feel about this, but I will never forget you. You will become the unique “Maomao” in my memory.

We will meet again tomorrow, even though that may never be possible.

My dearest friend.

Departure

Nimao’s departure was very unexpected and sudden... It was as if a drop of water had disappeared into the sea, nowhere to be found, or like a candle that had burned down to its last wick. He completely disappeared from the internet.

At first, his friends just thought he wasn’t feeling well and needed to rest for a while. But as time slowly passed, people seemed to realize there was a problem. It wasn’t until his phone was taken over by his family that we learned his illness wasn’t some ordinary sickness, but rather—[^1]

Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis

It was only then that most of his friends learned that the optimistic Nimao was suffering from a terminal illness, yet he had still left behind his cheerful presence on the internet.

On July 3rd, Nimao sank to the bottom of the sea in his sleep. ALS made him unable to breathe on his own. He was tired, and didn’t want to endure the physical and psychological pain anymore, so he closed his eyes and left this world forever.

“One day, we won’t need to say goodbye; we’ll only need to say goodnight.”

Goodnight, Nimao.

Contributors for this entry: _AloneStar_, Arista, Heibuzai

[^1]: Further reading: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis on Wikipedia.

LVNARIA MONITVR XXVI MENS LVLII A D MMXXVI OB NOXIVM MEDIC MORTVA SITO SINAE PAENE VTRVM LVNARIA NECNE LVNARIS VERITAS ERAT VOX IN VILLA COR IN RVINIS HIEMES IN III IN VINIVIS MEDICIS POSTEA TANDEM NON POTVIT FERRE EAM QVAE VOC MORBVM ET MORTVA EST REQVIESCAT I P[^1]

Lait’s Memories of the Forgotten Moon

Lait’s memories of Lvnaria date back a long time. Lait had always wanted to write a page for her, but due to Lait’s own procrastination, it dragged on until now, in 2026.

In Lait’s impression, Lvnaria was always suffering. During the more than half a year they knew each other well, she probably never had an easy time. Back then, she went to school far away from home, practically having to cross half of China, and her relationship with her family likely wasn’t very good either. Lait didn’t know what Lvnaria’s daily life was like, but Lait felt it must have been very arduous. In her final days, she tried to leave several times, and in the end, just as Lvnaria had anticipated, she succeeded.

Recalling that time now, it felt like Lvnaria was trying so hard to find an anchor to support herself, but ultimately failed.

Lait writes these words down now to remember Lvnaria.

Contributor for this entry: Lait Eimei

[^1]: This section is a pseudo-Latin epitaph; there may be intentional design choices or typos.

items.content_html:
Lighting the Lamp

If the night is too dark to see the road ahead, then I will be your lamp.
In May 2023, a friend and I started working on a psychological counseling project on an online platform. Perhaps my initial intention was not to help others, but to save myself. At that time, I was suffering from severe mental illness, living in confusion and despair every day—it was the darkest period of my life. Yet, I didn’t want to sink into the abyss, and I was desperate to find a way to redeem myself.
Then she appeared.
She came, gently and quietly, carrying the warm glow of orange light.
On that romantic day, May 20th.

The Lonely Star

She too was a child abandoned by the world.
She grew up in a deeply conservative family in Tongnan, Chongqing. Her father was a gambling addict, and her mother, a teacher. The parents’ preference for sons over daughters, along with the gloom of her family’s atmosphere, made her experience the bitterness of life at an age that should have been carefree. She never had a happy life: her parents’ scolding and beatings, her classmates’ ridicule, and the bullying from school thugs... Struggling to survive in the cracks of life, she had fallen into despair countless times and even attempted suicide. But she never allowed herself to be consumed by the darkness of human nature. She always shone with pure light, like a lonely star in the night sky.
Severe depression, acute anxiety, schizophrenia, ADHD… When my friend handed her over to me, I was completely shocked.
Could someone with such severe mental issues really be saved?

A Warm Current

I always felt that a sweet and kind child like Chinatsu deserved to be treated gently by the world. Even if everyone else abandoned her, I had to offer her that kindness.
I began talking to her every day, patiently comforting and guiding her, and gradually, I entered her world. She was an exceptionally talented person—fluent in English and Japanese, skilled in programming, and adept at AI illustration. She even had a keen financial mind and made significant money from cryptocurrency trading. Her network was extensive—she had even taken a photo with Satoshi Nakamoto. Our conversations were always filled with laughter. Two lonely souls, no longer isolated after meeting, found warmth in each other’s company. Her love, like a gentle current, nourished my heart, melting the long-frozen ice within.

Heaven’s Favor

“I’m a child blessed by heaven!” One day, Chinatsu told me excitedly, “I went to the hospital for a blood test, and the doctor said I had XX chromosomes, so I’m truly a girl!”
I was genuinely happy for her. It seemed as though fate had destined it—while one door had closed, another had opened for her. Perhaps the misfortune of her childhood had paved the way for a lifetime of happiness.
That day, she was overjoyed. She said, “One day, I hope to have my own children and live a happy life.”

Smile

After that, every time Chinatsu had suicidal thoughts, I would talk to her about the little joys of life, about our future. Over time, I stopped her from attempting suicide seven times.
With the combined efforts of Miss EnderCat and me, her condition miraculously improved. She became sunny and cheerful, and her face often showed a smile. At that moment, I had a premonition: maybe, just maybe, she would one day break free from the illness and be reborn.

The Fallen Flower Vanishes Without a Trace

In September, a very close friend of Chinatsu’s committed suicide, and Chinatsu, in her devastation, took pills to end her own life. This time, I couldn’t stop her. Although she was rescued, the damage from her previous suicide attempts had left severe aftereffects. Unfortunately, this time, it triggered the malignant growth of a benign brain tumor.
On the phone, Chinatsu cried to me, telling me how much pain she was in. My heart tightened hearing those words, but I couldn’t show my despair in front of her. Holding back my tears, I comforted her, “It will be alright… everything will be fine…”
After the call ended, I cried uncontrollably. It was at that moment I realized how important Chinatsu was to me. I couldn’t understand—how could such a wonderful child suffer this way? I simply couldn’t comprehend.
In her final days, she spoke to me about her childhood: “I remember when I was very young, I saw a handkerchief with cute designs on the table. I liked it so much that I reached for it, but my mother pulled my hand away and said, ‘Why would a boy like something so girly?’”
Her voice was weak, as though she was sobbing and reminiscing at the same time.
I cried my heart out, barely hearing her say, “In our next life, we must be together. I will wait for you.”
“Don’t be afraid,” I told her, “You’ll go to a beautiful place, warm and free of pain.”
On the other end of the line, there was only silence. Outside, the autumn wind blew, scattering the fallen flowers across the ground.

Reunion

It felt like someone had forcibly torn something out of me, leaving me numb and dejected. I still don’t understand why she left me behind, leaving me to wander this lonely world alone.
But it’s alright—she will wait for me. In the next life, we will be reunited.

Written by: A Ray of Sunshine for Chinatsu, Her Main Supporter
With the assistance of Miss EnderCat

Original

她寫給 lib 一抹陽光的遺書

她對 lib 一抹陽光說：『和你在一起的時光，是我 14 年以來最幸福的時候了』

『感謝末影貓小姐協助我幫助千夏』—lib 一抹陽光

『如果能有下輩子，我們一定要在一起』—鈴木千夏、lib 一抹陽光

items.content_html:
[!Tip] Reader’s note: For the sake of narrative completeness and coherence, this article has made an exception to retain the specific names of certain medications involved in episodes of drug overdose and sensitive medication use. Please do not imitate any of the actions described. If you feel unwell while reading, or experience any mental distress that may put you in danger, please stop reading immediately and seek help from a medical professional or the community.

Prologue

When Caijia and I were still in Chongqing, we often went to the restaurant downstairs for douhua rice. The owner recognized me every time. We’d become quite familiar with each other.

In Sichuan and Chongqing, douhua rice is always eaten with something spicy. The douhua itself has hardly any flavour.

Roasted Chili Sauce is pungent — every bite burns. Use a different condiment, and it takes on a different taste entirely.

Caijia, just a kid.

...To me, she was something like douhua.

Douhua has no flavour of its own. Whatever it is seasoned with, that is the flavour it takes on.

At the start of this year, I had the chance to return to Yubei. The owner was still there, greeting me with the same smile as always. But the person who once sat beside me was gone. There would be no one to share a bowl of douhua rice with me ever again.

Meeting

Caijia, just a kid. When I first got to know her in early 2024, it was only because she was dealing medications. What was it about her that drew me in...?

Back then, my profile picture was Gwyndolin from Dark Souls. When she asked if my avatar was from Dark Souls, I said yes, and that rush of joy — finding someone who shared the same interest — welled up inside me. I don’t quite know what compelled me, but I listened to so many of the stories she told, and felt a kind of pity for her. Perhaps it was also my own loneliness. We started calling each other sisters, growing closer and closer, and she changed her QQ profile picture to Yorshka — Gwyndolin’s sister.

She loved listening to Vocaloid songs and was always getting me to listen to all sorts of Vocaloid songs with her. She also loved Connect, the opening theme of Puella Magi Madoka Magica. She really did love Madoka. In her mind, everyone who died would be taken in by the Law of Cycles.[^1]

When Caijia was still in Hunan, I once ordered bubble tea delivery for her, and that was how I came to have her home address memorized. One time, I heard she had attempted suicide. In a panic, I gave the address to the local police. It was only when the police got back to me and said she had vomited up the pills she’d swallowed, right in front of them, that I felt some relief.

Soulmate

After we’d known each other for a while, I asked Caijia to come from Hunan to Chongqing to live with me. She really was just a kid, I suppose I “tricked” her into coming to my place.

Caijia said she’d come, no problem. But I wasn’t allowed to stop her from cutting herself, wasn’t allowed to stop her from overdosing, and wasn’t allowed to stop her from — doing compensated dating. All I could do was nod and go along with it, though in the end she never actually went through with that last one.

On 13th March, Caijia took the high-speed rail to come find me, but she’d bought a ticket to the remote Chongqingxi Station by mistake. Still, I took the metro there early and waited. When she finally arrived, the little lost soul got turned around again, and we spent ages searching for each other before we finally met.

(Holding hands when we met — mine on top, Caijia’s below.)

The moment I saw her, something inside me just felt: “Ah, this must be my soulmate.” Then I took her hand, and we rode the metro home.

Mint

With her connections as a medication dealer, we often bought pills and took them together. But I didn’t realize that this was only ever a fleeting kind of happiness.

I remember that before she came to see me, she’d always been curious about what clonazepam tasted like. I told her it tasted like mint, and you could even dissolve it under your tongue like candy.

The first night she stayed at my place, she couldn’t quite settle in — maybe it was the unfamiliar bed. She kept tossing and turning, so I tipped a clonazepam tablet into my mouth, leaned in, and kissed it into hers.

She seemed a little surprised. She hadn’t expected me to do that. When the taste registered, she realized it really was just like mint.

Conflict

Her emotions were very unstable. Whenever she broke down, she’d rush into the bathroom, lock the door, and cut her arms and thighs with a surgical blade. Sometimes it only took a disagreement between us for her to lock herself away and self-harm. I was completely helpless, and it drove me to the edge too, with nowhere to let it out. All I could do was hurt myself the way she did. The scars on my left hand are still clearly visible to this day.

Once, during a fight, I tried to wrestle the blade away from her because she was cutting herself. She wanted to jump off the building; I held her back. But I wasn’t as strong as her, and seeing that it wasn’t working, I had no choice but to call the police, hoping that would calm her down. That night, Caijia was taken to the Chongqing Mental Health Centre, where she stayed overnight.

The next day I went to see her, only to be told that non-family members weren’t allowed in for visits. So I waited outside, and waited, for her family to come. By evening, her grandfather and father arrived. I met with them; they went in and spoke with the doctors, and Caijia was released. Her family told me they hoped I could take good care of her, and reminded Caijia not to cause trouble. They stayed in Chongqing for one day and then went back. They actually seemed like decent people.

When Caijia and I were together, we sometimes talked about the future. I told her we should study Japanese together, that one day we’d go to Japan. I even discussed the plan with her mother and put together a proper proposal. Her mother treated her well enough. After I mediated for a while, her mother came to accept her gender identity and even bought her girls’ clothes. She was a gentle person.

Companionship

Looking back carefully now, the time I spent with her in Chongqing was probably less than two months. But she truly did have a happy time.

She loved eating Cuixiangmi instant noodle snacks, tomato-flavoured instant noodles, and Fujiya lollipops. Every trip to the convenience store, she’d grab a whole armful and carry it all home. She also loved going to McDonald’s with me, and tucked into Grilled Chicken Sandwiches and McFlurries.

(With her at McDonald’s)

Caijia loved watching anime. Back then, we finished watching Gushing over Magical Girls together. The title sounds like a magical girl story, but it’s actually overflowing with strange yuri elements. Her favourite character was Araga Kiwi, someone who looks like a fool on the surface but is actually hiding a great deal of strength. Sometimes, after taking our pills, we’d lie on the sofa, hook the laptop up to the TV, and keep enjoying the scenes.

We sometimes bought Rio premixed cocktails and watched Kamen Rider Build together. She quite liked it. The scene that left the deepest impression on her was Saruwatari Kazumi’s final transformation. His Hazard Level[^2] was too high, and in order to save his companions and the world, he forced a transformation using the Blizzard Knuckle, ultimately dying because it exceeded what a human body could withstand.

In our free time, we’d also play games together. She loved the Dark Souls series and its fan-made game, BLACK SOULS. We played Dark Souls 1 together — after all, it was our profile pictures that brought us together in the first place. I’d actually gotten into Dark Souls ages ago; I was a veteran. Sometimes, when she couldn’t beat a boss, I’d just sit right down at the computer desk:

“Let me handle this! There’s no boss your big sis can’t beat!”

We went to so many places, and those are all memories worth cherishing. Guanyinqiao,[^3] the Jiefangbei Pedestrian Street[^4]... we had fun in so many places. It was a kind of happiness I hadn’t felt in a long time — as if I wasn’t so alone anymore.

(Photo booth pictures taken with her near Jiefangbei Pedestrian Street)

I remember walking with her along the streets around Jiefangbei, around eight or nine in the evening, just holding her hand, and yet it felt like I had the whole world.

I remember that even though we were still underage, we snuck into a bar and ordered a drink. I think it was a Blue Margarita[^5] — my first drink at a bar, and hers too.

I remember one time we went out to eat, over by the shopping district near Chongqing Central Park.[^6] We’d probably been cooped up at home too long and just wanted something nice.

“Where shall we go this time? Jiefangbei? Or Central Park?”

“Let’s go to Central Park — it’s closer.”

“Whatever you say~”

Downstairs from Paradise Walk, there was a big figurine shop. Caijia and I browsed around in there for ages — so many cute figurines, all of which we wanted and none of which we could afford.

(A date at Brew King Bistro on Paradise Walk)

So we went upstairs to Brew King Bistro and sat down to eat. It was quite a feast, and Caijia was very happy. Though perhaps girls really do have four stomachs — one for the main course, one for snacks, one for fruit, and one for drinks. After the meal, we left the Paradise Walk and went looking for something to drink.

At Naixue[^7], Caijia and I placed our order and sat down to wait until the staff called our number. Right at that moment, her mother happened to call to ask how Caijia was doing. And that’s how this photo came to be:

(Caijia in front of Naixue on Paradise Walk)

Come to think of it, we’d heard there was a maimai machine at a nearby arcade, but since we were both too socially anxious, we never once tried it.

Plushies

29th April was my birthday, and Caijia had prepared a plushie for me well in advance. It was a... big shark.

But Caijia, clumsy as she was, plunged the knife in a bit too hard while opening the package and accidentally stabbed the poor sharkie to death.

Caijia was a little upset.

“It’s okay, it’ll be fine,” I comforted her.

While she turned and went back to her room, I dug out the sewing kit my mother had left behind, followed a tutorial online, and stitched the sharkie back together.

“Look, look — it’s alive again!”

But Caijia still felt guilty, thinking it was her fault for ruining my birthday present. Later, to make up for it, she bought me a Kuromi plushie.

(The Kuromi plushie Caijia gave me)

Although the sharkie is no longer with me. That Kuromi plushie — I still carry it with me to this day.

Swarm

She kept listening to some “doctor” in the overdose community, and after hearing that amantadine was good, she’d often buy it behind my back and take it, which left her in a terrible mental state. She said she kept seeing hallucinations — seeing insects — and I had no idea what to do. All I could do was throw away her pills and stay by her side.

I’m really scared of bugs...

The hallucinations from “goodnight”[^8] are really strange and terrifying.

Swarms of insects pouring out from under the bed, the floor covered in shattered glass from my glasses...

Goodnight — what irony...

(Excerpted from Caijia’s tweets)

Then there was another time... I think it was because I didn’t want her using the surgical blade to hurt herself anymore, and we ended up in a physical struggle. She beat me black and blue. I was falling apart and just wanted to go to my room for some quiet. She thought I was going to do something stupid and broke the lock on my bedroom door, then came crashing in.

Both our families found out about this, and they demanded that Caijia go back to Hunan. But I couldn’t bear to let her go, seeing the state she was in, and Caijia felt bad about what she’d done and couldn’t bear to leave me either. So together we made up a lie. We told them she had gone somewhere else to visit a friend, and she actually stayed on at my place.

Insomnia

On 4th May, it was drizzling in Yubei. I’d been up all night gaming.

Caijia came up to me and asked: “You hasn’t been overdosing lately, sis... What’s going on...?”

Looking back, maybe I’d unconsciously felt that she was in too bad a state and thought it would be better not to touch the stuff anymore. I can’t quite remember now. But she brought it up, and I thought, well, if that’s what she wants.

“I guess you’re right. If you want some, I’ll go buy some with you.” I said.

On the way home from buying the pills, she picked up a parcel — a box of empty capsule shells. According to her, if you crushed the pills and put them inside, they wouldn’t taste so bad. We took them together after that.

...What on earth was I doing...

Then I felt like I couldn’t sleep, so I took some clonazepam and tried to lie down in bed. But right around that time, her phone and ID card went missing.

“We’ll look for them later. I’m so tired, so sleepy... let me just rest for a bit.”

Maybe it was because the clonazepam hit too hard. By the time I woke up again, I was already in an ambulance. Caijia leaned in close and told me she’d been calling my name but couldn’t wake me, so she used my phone to call 120.

“What happened... I’m awake, aren’t I? Just a bit drowsy...” Since there was nothing seriously wrong, I paid the ambulance fee, and Caijia and I went home to keep resting.

When I woke up again it was three or four in the morning, and I realized my phone was gone. Using iCloud’s Find My feature, I saw it was located at the police station. I threw on some clothes and hurried over, and sure enough, there she was.

She was wearing clothes I’d never seen before. I later found out it was because she’d been running around outside wearing only a top, and someone had brought her to the station.

“Sis, what are you doing at the police station? Aren’t you coming home? Let’s go home and sleep!” My own head was still a bit foggy.

So I took my phone back, held Caijia’s hand, and we went home.

Shattered

“I still want to play games. Can you still play Dark Souls?” Caijia asked me after we got home.

So much had been happening, and I still felt so drowsy, so desperate to rest. All I could do was try to soothe her for a moment, then turn off the lights and go to sleep.

When I woke up this time, it was around 6 in the morning. The property management staff came knocking on my door in a rush, but didn’t tell me what had happened. They just told me to hurry downstairs.

I went downstairs in a daze. A few people who looked like security guards — or maybe police — led me forward.

“What’s going on... it’s so early. Where’s my sis?”

They led me to the sports area in front of the property management office. In the corner, there was a motionless figure.

My mind went blank. What is this...? Who is this...?

The figure had its back to me. I looked carefully at the top she was wearing — the only piece of clothing on her — and suddenly jolted awake from the haze.

“Sis! What happened to you! Sis! Answer me! Please, just respond...” I kept calling out to her, hoping for any kind of reaction.

But there was no response.

The security guards around her wouldn’t let me get close.

“Oh dear, she’s already gone. The ambulance already came, took one look, and left. There’s no point trying to save her now.” The woman nearby sighed, then turned away, unwilling to deal with me any further.

The police urged me to leave too, saying I needed to go do something or other, telling me to stop looking.

But I couldn’t bring myself to go. My legs felt like they were filled with lead — so heavy — and I stood rooted to the spot.

They walked over and turned Caijia onto her back. Only then could I finally see her face.

The tears wouldn’t stop.

“I’m sorry... your big sis didn’t protect you...”

Absence

After I finished giving my statement, the officers at the station were worried I’d have a breakdown — that I’d be alone in Chongqing, unable to cope, and try to end my own life. So I was kept there for two days, until my mother came all the way from Xinjiang to Chongqing to take me out.

“Have you eaten?”

“I don’t want to eat anything. I have absolutely no appetite...”

That’s what I said, but later, I still went to the McDonald’s downstairs and bought a McFlurry.

“Caijia... she loved these.”

“Don’t bring that up.”

Walking back towards home, I deliberately made my way to that little corner of the sports area. It seemed to have been cleaned up. You couldn’t tell at all what had happened there just the morning before.

A life. Cordoned off with police tape, covered with a tarp, the crowd dispersed. Before long, it was as though the whole thing had never happened.

Those who witnessed the tragedy — would any of them take it to heart? They all scattered soon enough.

The crowds came and went as always, laughter and footsteps interweaving without pause. In the end, I alone remembered what had happened in this corner where parents and children play.

Yubei

When Caijia left, she still had two packs of unfinished tomato instant noodles.

Because of what had happened, my family took me away and kept me under watch. Later, due to family circumstances, I left Chongqing for good.

That home in Yubei is a home I can never return to. It holds my youth, and it holds the most painful thing that has ever happened to me.

In March, I went back to the old place in Yubei. I brought her a few bottles of compound liquorice tablets.

I miss the days of mixing premixed cocktails with cola, taking liquorice tablets and DXM. And that little path we’d walk to pick up parcels.

Does she remember any of this? Wherever she is — has she found happiness...?

In the blink of an eye, the name Yubei has been fading with the wind. The signs bearing Yubei’s name have been taken down one by one, replaced by Liangjiang New Area.[^9]

But that story remains forever in a Yubei that can never be returned to.

Last Chapter

The overdose community had too great an influence on Caijia. If not for that, she might have had a decent future.

Caijia, just a kid.

...To me, she was something like douhua.

Whoever she was with — that’s who she’d become...

After Caijia was gone, I never ordered anything else at bars. Only Blue Margaritas. Every time I go to a bar, that’s all I order. Even though I don’t actually like drinking them at all... the rim of the glass is lined with sea salt — bitter and astringent.

But it was my first drink at a bar, and it was hers too.

Contributor for this entry: Poetry Luna

[^1]: See the final episode of the Puella Magi Madoka Magica TV anime, My Very Best Friend.

[^2]: In Kamen Rider Build, the “Hazard Level” is a measure of one’s power. The higher the value, the greater the strength, but also the greater the risk of losing control.

[^3]: Now part of the Liangjiang New Area commercial district in Chongqing.

[^4]: The Jiefangbei–Chaotianmen commercial district, located in Yuzhong District, Chongqing, also considered the city centre.

[^5]: A cocktail created by bartender Jean Durasa in memory of his lover, Margaret, who died in an accident.

[^6]: Now part of the Liangjiang New Area commercial district in Chongqing. Chongqing Park Paradise Walk, Chongqing Joy City, and Wuyue Plaza (Central Park, Chongqing) are all located here.

[^7]: Formerly Nayuki, renamed Naìsnow in 2025.

[^8]: In Chinese, “goodnight” (晚安，wǎn’ān) is a near-homophone of amantadine (金刚烷胺，jīn gāng wǎn’àn), the drug mentioned earlier. The word here carries both meanings.

[^9]: Refers to the administrative redistricting of Chongqing on November 5, 2025, in which the greater part of the former Yubei District was merged into Liangjiang New Area.

items.content_html:
Tenderness in the Corner

NIGHT was a trans girl who endured a life of hardship. She had been shrouded in what seemed an endless gloom, yet her heart never ceased reaching towards the light.

The family she was born into was not a happy one. Her parents never truly taught her how to be a decent person. It was books and visual novels that taught her love, courage, and all manner of virtue.

Her reading list ranged from works of great depth and fate such as Faust and One Hundred Years of Solitude, to stories brimming with imagination and adventure like The Adventures of Tom Sawyer and Gulliver’s Travels.

Visual novels were also a vital source of nourishment for her spirit. Within those worlds woven from text and choices, where branching storylines intertwined, she gradually formed her own values. Among the many titles she encountered, the one that left the deepest mark was the Rance series—and the character she loved most dearly was Shizuka Masou. Shizuka was a powerful and gifted magic user, carrying the trauma of her father’s early death and an obsession with vengeance, fighting against fate while holding fast to her own moral compass. Cold and distant on the surface, she concealed boundless tenderness and goodwill within. Shizuka’s strength of character profoundly influenced NIGHT, and so, throughout her life, she strove to embody the resilience, kindness, and quiet tenderness that Shizuka never easily revealed to others.

And yet, this resilient, kind, and gentle girl wrote the following confession:

I want to become a person who is pure, flawless, and noble… but it seems that is no longer possible.

My heart is already filled with filth, and the wrongs I have committed can never be undone.

Defiance

NIGHT’s father was a man who bullied the weak and cowered before the strong. She had been beaten by him since childhood. But eventually, he no longer dared to lay a hand on her. Not because he had changed, but because she had relentlessly pushed herself to exercise, making her body strong.

On the pages of a diary already yellowed with age, her training results were recorded in clear black ink:

Push-ups × 85

Squats × 110

Calf raises × 50

Sit-ups × 60

Years of persistent training gave her body the strength to stand against her father. At last, she could protect herself and her mother.

“You can call me a unfilial son if you want, but back then, I protected my mum. That’s one of the few things I can actually be proud of.”

Unable to subdue her with physical violence any longer, her father continued to wear down her dignity with degrading words.

I confronted my father: “Why did you have to cheat? Why did you have to betray us?”

He said, “All men are like this. Someday you’ll be just like me.”

I said I wouldn’t—I could never be like him, not in a lifetime. But he just said I was too young to understand.

Malice from Every Side

According to NIGHT’s own recollection, around the time of her senior high school entrance exams, she faced extreme bullying at school. Perhaps because she could not bear to revisit those memories, she initially wrote the year as 2019, only realizing after putting it down that it should have been 2020.

At school, everyone mocked her for her unclear speech, imitating the way she talked to humiliate her. The experience left a deep scar—so much so that, from then on, she became acutely self-conscious about her voice. She grew unwilling to speak at all; no matter who called out to her, she would not answer. She no longer wanted to go to school, but at home she found no understanding either.

Her family humiliated her, saying things like “If you won’t study, go haul bricks at a construction site,” “You need to make something of yourself—if you can’t, you might as well be dead,” “How are you still alive,” and “Leave him a little knife so he can kill himself.”

She had no words to answer them and could only cry alone. There was nothing she could do, because her parents spent the entire day berating and dragging her down, and most of her time was consumed in these exhausting confrontations.

She spent half a year in utter futility. It was not until the day before her exams that she finally returned to school. Her parents threatened that if she failed to get into high school, they would send her out to work.

Despite the enormous pressure, she managed to gain admission to a local high school. But when the time came to start, she was terrified of being humiliated again. Though she still wanted to attend, the dread of reliving that nightmare ultimately led her to drop out.

Even after dropping out, her parents refused to let her stay home alone. They cut off her living expenses as leverage, coercing her into following them to Guangdong to work in their new venture.

Her parents had scraped together 300,000 yuan and opened a small textile dyeing factory in Dongguan. The workers were all relatives, and none of them were paid.

NIGHT was also made to work there. The work itself was not strenuous, but the hours were excruciatingly long, and she received no pay whatsoever. After a while, she refused to continue and locked herself in her room, eating and drinking nothing—and so she was constantly hungry. In the end, she had no choice but to work from time to time, if only to get a meal.

Yet even at work, she was subjected to a constant stream of abuse. Her family called her worthless, and that crushing hostility only deepened the weight on her mind.

Light in the Dead of Night

During those days in Guangdong, she was utterly alone. Her only chance to download visual novels was late at night, using her parents’ mobile data while they slept.

She had no social contact at all—not even online. Her sole companions, day after day, were the characters on the screen, carrying her through each agonising day.

She envied Rance, who could always set off on carefree adventures, whose friends were always by his side no matter what he did.

She envied Tear[^1], who could become the wind and protect the one she loved.

She envied Tomoya[^2], too—an ordinary person who lived a plain yet happy life.

A lot of my dreams took shape during that time—like wanting to be happy, things like that. But in the end, I suppose it was never really possible…

Even though I couldn’t get enough to eat back then, had no friends at all, and was berated all day long.

I still miss that time. I miss every day those fictional characters spent by my side. I’m grateful they kept me company through all that loneliness.

Those lonely, painful days dragged on and on, but those games were among the very few lights that kept shining on me.

And yet I couldn’t keep up with that light, and just kept sinking further and further down…

The God Above

NIGHT had a strong religious inclination, and so there was always a figure she called “the God Above” in her heart.

Though she never knew who the God Above was, she held fast to the belief that one day, the God Above would come to save her.

In earlier times, she would always pray to the God Above—praying for someone, praying for tomorrow.

When she was hungry, she would pray to the God Above.

Before meals, she would give thanks for the God Above’s protection, believing it was the God Above who had spared her from hunger.

Sometimes, she also felt the God Above was terribly unfair, unwilling to spare her even the smallest grace.

But after a certain event, she never prayed again.

Because she came to feel that the God Above would never shine any light upon her.

“The God Above”"]]} />

To Live

NIGHT also spent a great deal of time contemplating the subject of life itself.

In the summer of 2021, the bitterness of life overwhelmed her, and she attempted to free herself from this world. Two years later, looking back on what had happened, she felt that her life had actually been getting better—and that, paradoxically, she had lost the courage to die.

She read Yu Hua’s To Live and came upon the line: “People live for the sake of living itself, not for anything beyond living.” She then wrote the following:

The word “people” in this sentence is a broad category—meaning you can substitute any specific person.

For example, Gagarin was a person, so you could conclude that Gagarin lived for the sake of living itself, not for anything beyond living—which is obviously wrong. The same substitution works with any historical figure.

But if the meaning of living is simply living, then that amounts to saying living has no meaning—just as saying the meaning of snowfall is snowfall. From this, you could conclude that all those historical figures lived meaningless lives.

NIGHT said these words to herself, but the word “living” only grew heavier because of them. At night, she wiped away her tears in secret, leaving herself with nothing more than the simplest of sentences:

Tomorrow, I must keep on living.

She wondered: how would she have to live in order to say, as Wittgenstein did on his deathbed, “Tell them I’ve had a wonderful life”?

A few days later, she wrote:

Well… if I were to die, all I could say would be, “I lived an unhappy life, full of regrets.”

Sadly, as time went on, NIGHT came to feel that she had been living in the past all along. What she chased was a happiness that had already been, and she realized those days could never return.

Perhaps I died back in those long-gone, unreachable days, and surviving was nothing but an accident.

Just as the final line of The Great Gatsby says:

“So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past.”

A Hot Bath

In her daily life, the happiest moment was always when she took a hot bath.

And so she would always stay in there for a very, very long time… even if she did nothing at all, just letting the hot water pour over her.

And so, she made a small, quiet wish:

She hoped that one day, her home would have a rain showerhead—one that fell like rain. That way, she wouldn’t have to hold the showerhead in her hand.

And then… playing music while she bathed. That alone would make her happy.

“Oh my… I’ve never even used a bathtub,” she said.

“If only I had a thermostat bathtub… it would be so lovely to just soak in it forever.”

Flight and Respite

In the spring of 2024, she could no longer endure her parents and their small factory in Guangdong, and so she set out on a journey of escape.

She settled into a long-term stay at a hotel in the Yangtze River Delta. Though things were somewhat calmer, life still refused to let her be.

“Bitter liquor, much like a bitter life—hard to swallow, yet impossible to refuse.”

While staying at the hotel, she slept so deeply that the staff mistook it for a suicide attempt. Though the misunderstanding caused a bit of trouble, she felt, in it, a small touch of care.

If only I really had a home, I wouldn’t have to stay in a hotel.

Maybe I’m dreaming. I really do have a home—hazy, drifting. I must be dreaming.

Even while drifting from place to place, she held on to the goodness in her heart. She took in a penniless, homeless trans girl, and paid out of her own pocket to cover the girl’s travel fare so she could travel on.

She had wanted to go further, but she was tired.

I had planned to go to Beijing, to Tianjin, or somewhere even further.

But I’m too tired. I’ll just settle down in Nanjing. I don’t want to go anywhere any more.

Final Words

She did not want her emotions controlled by medication.

She threw away all her pills.

She wanted love, yet could not feel it.

She wanted to leave, yet had lost the ability to make decisions—and so she cast the dice of fate.

She never said what the dice showed. But she decided to listen to fate once more.

Yet she was too weary of living, and no amount of alcohol could suppress the despair in her heart…

We will never see each other again.

But I think, in the end, a small farewell is still needed—

My friend, thank you for appearing in my life.

Thank you for staying by my side all this time.

When you wake tomorrow morning, it will be a brand-new day.

It’s just that I no longer have a tomorrow. I can no longer pray for yours.

So this time, I sincerely wish you happiness.

Please forget me.

And finally, goodbye…

Perhaps she left because of that belief—that her happiness had been forever stranded in the past…

Just as the ending of her beloved The Great Gatsby says:

So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past.

A Belated Greeting

A year after she passed away, we heard from her once more:

This is a scheduled post from 2024.

Today is my birthday—please wish me a happy birthday~

A year has gone by. How is everyone doing?

Dear NIGHT, the world may be getting worse, but we have never stopped trying.

Even if the world has not become a better place, we keep striving to become better ourselves.

And—happy birthday.

[^1]: A character from That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime.

[^2]: Tomoya Okazaki, a character from the visual novel CLANNAD by Key.

items.content_html:
Cat

Enchanted Golden Cat. Well, just hearing a name like that, you can already know, this had to be a cat who loved Minecraft.

Perhaps because she had such an adorable name, she often made jokes about it herself.

Once, a mutual on Twitter was hosting a follower milestone giveaway, and among the prizes was a Minecraft apple keychain in transgender flag colours.

She said, “I am the Enchanted Golden Apple!” and attached a super fierce kitty sticker.

Another time, someone joked that they were short on money and wanted to “rob a bank[^1] in cyberspace,” calling for people to reply with “1” to join in.

She playfully replied, “1! I’ve got an Enchanted Golden Apple!”

What a mischievous little cat she was.

Cats

In May 2023, she welcomed a kitten of her own.

“I have my own kitten now!”

It was a tiny kitten, new to its surroundings and a little scared of her at first.

But before long, the two of them became close friends.

In Memory

Her passing came suddenly, without any warning at all.

She was very skilled at playing Fall Guys, and had unlocked all of its achievements on Steam at the time.

After her departure, among those who came to mourn her, there were these words from RusndageSNF:

I suddenly thought of you again… If you were still here, how wonderful that would be. We could play Fall Guys duos together.

I’d even give you my account... Why... why didn’t I meet you sooner…?

How did I never get to know you, you little trans girl who played Fall Guys…

May there be the games you loved on the other side, the Enchanted Golden Apples you cherished, and the sound of music drifting through the clouds of Sky...

[^1]: The “bank robbery” joke is a reference to a scene from Blue Archive, see Chapter 1 Episodes 13–15 of the game, or Episode 4 of the anime TV series adaptation.

items.content_html:
The Transit Enthusiast

MocaKawai took her name from Aoba Moca of BanG Dream!. Whichever Moca you have in mind, both are impossibly endearing, both a little scatterbrained — the kind of person you can’t help but look at twice.

As a transit enthusiast, Moca played a wide range of simulation and management games, including Rail Route and Cities: Skylines. She would often stare at route maps, lost in thought, designing the perfect transit network for some imaginary city.

She also played Fall Guys and Among Us. She was always warm and lively in the comment sections of her videos, sometimes sharing little tips and tricks with her friends there.

Having lived in Sanya for most of her life, Moca knew the city’s public transit system inside and out. She filmed a great many transit-related videos, the majority of which were front-window POVs of Sanya’s bus routes.

For those who follow transit POVs, what matters most is not the footage itself, it is the mood. A different route, a different hour, a different state of mind, and the POV becomes something else entirely, something hard to put into words. Moca understood this. She gave each of her POV videos a carefully chosen title, passing on that sense of being there to her friends:

“Express from the two major hubs straight to the westernmost tip of Sanya”

“Drifting into nightfall in the hypnotic sway of a sightseeing route at China’s southernmost point”

“Racing uphill through a downpour”

“Chasing the sunset on the expressway!”

In September 2022, confined at home during the COVID-19 pandemic, Moca created a schematic map of Sanya’s rapid transit network. Nearly a year later, she revisited and refined the map, adding several intercity routes to the original design.

Her love for transit was much like the titles she wrote. Every bit of it sincere, and quietly romantic.

Escape from the Island

In the summer of 2023, Moca’s mental health deteriorated sharply for a number of reasons, and she began to overdose. The pressure of her final year of high school soon followed. At the end of August, a suicide attempt landed her in the ICU. She survived, but things did not truly get better. After being discharged, she lost her partner, lost her friends, and her physical condition worsened.

Afterwards, Moca took a leave of absence from school. She had few friends in Sanya, so she decided to travel to the Yangtze River Delta — to wander through cities she had never been to before. The trip allowed her to meet friends she had only known online, and for a while, it eased some of her pain.

Tried savoury doufunao (tofu pudding) for the first time? Not really my thing. Long live sweet doufunao!

McDonald’s! It’s so much cheaper outside Sanya, I’m so jealous…

The sticky rice is delicious! Totally different from what you get in Sanya!

For a brief moment, she had escaped the island — not just the geographical one, but the one inside her mind.

But after returning to Hainan, the darkness closed in again. Her continued misuse of medication only made things worse. The substance she had purchased during her travels ultimately took her life after she returned to Sanya. She did not make it through that autumn.

“It’s so damp… or maybe that’s just my tears…”

Rain or shine, silence or rush hour... All of it was scenery that Moca wanted to share with us. Every route she cared about, she recorded with care and posted for her fellow transit lovers to see.

She always liked to sit at the very front of the bus, watching the road unfold through the wide windscreen ahead.

This last ride, though, had no final stop.

items.content_html:
Introduction

There are always people like this in the world, quietly giving up their last bit of hope to help others.

Mo was one of them.

Her family of origin was not a happy one. The care and affection that others could easily take for granted felt to her like an unreachable illusion.

We may never know what her family was like, or what she went through in her life. By the time we were able to truly “see” her, she had already lost her attachment to the possibilities of the future.

Since early 2023, Mo had begun thinking about purchasing various drugs for the purpose of ending her life. At the same time, regardless of the risks to her accounts and her own safety, she distributed the money she had worked hard to earn to people through various channels. Perhaps they were fellow victims of scams, peers struggling with credit card debt, or simply desperate strangers with nowhere else to turn…

Many of those she helped were grateful for her selflessness. Of course, there were also a few opportunists who took advantage of her kindness.

There were also people who pitied her and called her foolish.

“Is there no one you love?”

“No… there isn’t.”

There’s so much I want to say, but I can’t seem to say any of it. At last, I can be free.

Living has been so painful. I don’t even know what to say anymore. If I had been born into a normal family, if I could have felt a little more love, would my life have turned out completely differently?

Sadly, there are too many “ifs”, and not a single one came true. I hope that in my next life, I can be born into a happy family—at the very least, not like this.

Thank you to everyone who has cared about me all this time. I hope all of you who see this can continue to live happily.

Before she left, she gave all her hope and warmth to others, and then said goodbye to this world in a cold and quiet loneliness.

The world has lost a child in pain, and with her, a clumsy kind of gentleness.

Contributors for this entry: One Among Us, Bai, Linghao, Zaolin, silvicky

Introduction

Coin was a warm and free-spirited girl. She loved Yoimiya from Genshin Impact, so we often called her Yoimiya in our daily lives.

Zhuojiu, Liangxiu, and Sha’er were the people she cared about the most.

Coin liked green onions and mashed potatoes. She always took great care of us. The meals she made were more than just food; they carried her warmth and sincerity.

Her family situation was difficult. In order to become financially independent, she spent some time providing in-game escort services in Delta Force to earn money.

From beginning to end, she bore heavy pressure from her family and never received the care and understanding she deserved.

The passing of her friend Haruka made her already fragile mental state even worse. She was overwhelmed with grief and inner turmoil. We were afraid she might follow the same path, but in the end, we couldn’t hold her back. Life weighed her down completely. She often suffered from insomnia and could only manage to fall asleep with the help of medication.

She had borrowed a significant amount through Huabei (a consumer credit service by Ant Group); most of it was not for herself, but rather for her friends. She was always attentive and sensitive when it came to those she cared about.

When she first arrived in Wuhan, she brought almost nothing with her. When she departed, she did not leave a single belonging at her friend’s place, yet she left herself behind in Wuhan forever.

When we returned to the room where she had once slept, it was empty. There was almost nothing that could represent her, only a piece of clothing she had worn and the psychiatric medication she had taken.

It felt as if she were still with us, yet we could never find her again.

She must have been truly in despair. When she was found, she lay quietly in a hotel in a distant city, beyond any help.

She left without a sound, without saying anything at all.

No more pain. On the other side, you are forever that free-spirited girl. May you always be at peace.
